papers.title: SingPro 2.0: a proteomics-centric knowledge base for single-cell multimodal profiling.
papers.summary: SingPro 2.0 upgrades a single-cell proteomics database into a proteomics-centric knowledge base for protein-inclusive multimodal profiling: 814 studies, ~81.5 million cells, 29 tissues, 44 diseases, spanning five omics modalities and 12 technologies, with cross-modality visualization. Freely accessible without login, it supports cell-atlas construction and disease-mechanism studies.

papers.title: Tumor gasdermin E acts as a rheostat to limit apoptotic cell survival and mutagenesis in anticancer immune environments.
papers.summary: Gasdermin E (GSDME), frequently silenced in tumors, limited caspase activity before membrane rupture during apoptosis. Losing GSDME let DNA-damaged cells survive caspase-activated DNase attack, propagating mutated clones; TCGA tumors with low GSDME and high immune signatures showed higher mutational burden, framing GSDME as a rheostat over death-versus-survival outcomes.

papers.title: Toward transgenic multicellular parasites: CRISPR-Cas12a germline editing of Schistosoma mansoni eggs as key to success.
papers.summary: A CRISPR-Cas12a ribonucleoprotein approach achieved efficient homology-directed insertion of a donor template into a Schistosoma mansoni safe-harbor site. Electroporated eggs produced EGFP-positive transgenic parasites that developed through the life cycle, with chromosomal integration and stable transformation across filial generations, enabling functional genomics in platyhelminths.

papers.title: Remodeling of mitochondrial dynamics by metabolic pathways couples to oncogenic growth in GNAS (Gα(s)) mutant pancreas cancer.
papers.summary: In KRAS(G12D)-mutant pancreatic cancer carrying GNAS(R201C/H) comutations, hyperactive GNAS kept mitochondria fused rather than fissed, supporting tumor growth. The GNAS-regulated branched-chain amino acid pathway, TCA cycle, and aspartate metabolism converge on NAD+/NADH metabolites to promote mitochondrial fusion, uncoupling mitochondrial morphology from canonical KRAS-driven remodeling.

papers.title: Functional diversification of CsCAD14 orchestrates synergistic phenylpropanoid biosynthesis to defend gray blight disease in tea plants.
papers.summary: Tea CsCAD14 exhibits dual enzymatic activity, synthesizing both monolignols and hydroxycinnamic acids that synergistically inhibit Pestalotiopsis (gray blight). A nonsynonymous mutation abolishing dual activity tracked with susceptibility, and evolutionary analysis suggests an L192V substitution drove CAD neofunctionalization from single-enzyme algae to dual-activity land plants during terrestrialization.

papers.title: Deep learning-enhanced single-shot triorganelle STED-FLIM imaging of lipid dynamics in living cells.
papers.summary: A single-shot STED-FLIM workflow pairs Nile Red analogs with deep-learning demultiplexing and VGG16-UNet segmentation to resolve ER, lipid droplets, and mitochondria from one acquisition in living cells. It captured coordinated tri-organellar lipid remodeling during lipid stress, including ferroptosis- and apoptosis-associated nanoscale and microenvironmental transitions.

papers.title: Speech clocks decode dementia phenotypes, social exposome, and biological aging.
papers.summary: A speech clock trained on acoustic and linguistic features from 2,928 participants across five Latin American countries generated speech-age gaps that differentiated controls, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and frontotemporal dementia. Speech age gaps correlated with p-tau217, brain-clock measures, epigenetic age, and social exposome, offering a scalable, low-cost aging biomarker candidate.

papers.title: Silver(I)-mediated amide-to-ester transformation on unprotected peptides for protein chemical synthesis and engineering.
papers.summary: A silver(I)-mediated amide-to-ester transformation using an N,S-benzylidene thioacetal scaffold converts backbone amides of unprotected peptides into salicylaldehyde esters in aqueous acetic acid without epimerization. Demonstrated across many peptides and mirror-image histone syntheses (H2A-H4), it provides a programmable platform for peptide and protein chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Restoring brain functions in the Mo-blo mouse model of Menkes disease with copper nanoclusters.
papers.summary: Copper nanoclusters, ultrasmall enough to cross the blood-brain barrier, treated Menkes disease (ATP7A-deficient) Mo-blo mice. Daily subcutaneous dosing markedly improved survival, normalized cuproprotein activities, and restored cognitive and motor function, delivering copper to brain cuproproteins where conventional copper-histidine therapy fails, suggesting the first brain-directed therapy for this fatal disorder.

papers.title: Predicting and finding geroprotective compounds through modulating conserved longevity-associated aging modules.
papers.summary: Aging transcriptomes in C. elegans were deconstructed into coexpression modules modulated by life-span-extending interventions. These longevity-associated modules predicted and validated 10 geroprotective compounds (7 previously unreported); top candidates' transcriptomes targeted the modules, and several conserved modules in mice correlated with frailty, providing a generalizable geroprotector-discovery framework.

papers.title: A noncanonical function of the tyrosine degradation enzyme FAH drives CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance in breast cancer.
papers.summary: Fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase (FAH), a cytosolic tyrosine catabolism enzyme, translocated to the nucleus upon CDK4/6 inhibition in breast cancer models, interacted with CDK9, and drove resistance. Nuclear FAH was enriched in relapsed patient tumors, and CDK9 inhibition reversed resistance, establishing FAH as a biomarker and CDK9 as a therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.title: Multiobjective V(H)H discovery through integrated high-throughput screening and AlphaFold3-guided structural prioritization.
papers.summary: A pipeline combining high-throughput yeast display, deep sequencing, and AlphaFold3-guided structural triage identified polyspecific VHH single-domain antibodies against conserved epitopes of long-chain alpha-neurotoxins from multiple snake species. Optimized variants retained broad binding and toxin neutralization, a framework applicable where antigenic variation demands broad-coverage biologics, including antivenoms.

papers.title: A forward genetics platform for papillomavirus research.
papers.summary: A forward-genetics platform for human papillomavirus uses concordant virus libraries in which each mutant particle encapsidates its encoding plasmid, linking genotype to phenotype and achieving ~2,500-fold enrichment of an L1 mutant. Selection recovered antibody-escape mutants, distinguishing two L1 neutralizing-antibody epitopes, enabling vaccine and antiviral studies.

papers.title: Contrasting modes of intron evolution in an evolutionarily distinct eukaryotic lineage revealed by comparative genomics of ciliated protists.
papers.summary: Comparative genomics of ciliated protists revealed intron evolution dominated by loss, with deep-branching lineages undergoing massive loss and almost no gain. Tiny 3n introns are preferentially retained when generating premature termination codons, likely triggering nonsense-mediated decay of aberrant transcripts, while spliceosome core components are conserved but regulatory factors vary by lineage.

papers.title: Collapse of embryonic identities and emergence of functional diversity during motor neuron maturation.
papers.summary: Temporal single-nucleus multiome sequencing of mouse motor neurons showed embryonic subtypes comprising dozens of column/pool-specific clusters collapse their identity during maturation, then re-diversify into adult alpha, gamma, and type-3 neurons innervating different muscle fiber types. Neuronal subtype diversity transforms completely during maturation to meet changing functional demands.

papers.title: Distinct phases of immune system programming during ART-suppressed immunodeficiency virus infection.
papers.summary: Longitudinal single-cell transcriptomics of SIV-infected, ART-treated macaques revealed biphasic immune remodeling: an acute interferon-driven phase tracking viral replication that largely resolves with suppression, and a later phase (54-66 weeks) of TGF-beta/NF-kappaB signaling and bone-marrow-restricted inflammatory monocyte bursts, with blunted interferon responses in gut lymph nodes potentially supporting reservoir persistence.

papers.title: USP-48 enables insulin-mediated longevity and modulates the mitochondrial stress response.
papers.summary: A genome-wide double-RNAi screen in C. elegans identified USP-48 as required for the longevity of insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutants under mitochondrial stress. USP-48 acts mainly in the hypodermis, cooperates with DVE-1 to regulate the mitochondrial unfolded protein response largely independently of ATFS-1, and promotes histone H2B deubiquitination, linking ubiquitination to metabolism-dependent longevity.

papers.title: Vpu protects HIV-infected cells from antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis by counteracting tetherin.
papers.summary: HIV-1 Vpu mutations impairing tetherin antagonism increased virion accumulation on infected cells and their susceptibility to antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis; effects were lost in tetherin-knockout cells and restored by inducible tetherin. Vpu thereby shields infected cells from Fc-mediated effector functions, amplifying tetherin's antiviral impact beyond its inhibition of virus release.

papers.title: Biphasic SMN condensates safeguard stress-induced cytoplasmic mislocalization of splicing RNPs.
papers.journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
papers.summary: Molecular crowding stress rapidly and reversibly condensed cytoplasmic SMN into S-bodies that sequester mislocalized spliceosomal snRNPs along microtubules; during recovery these split into Janus bodies that promote snRNP clearance. Spinal muscular atrophy models failed to assemble S-bodies, revealing impaired molecular-crowding tolerance as a disease hallmark.

papers.title: Improving the differentiation capability of porcine induced pluripotent stem cells by using the additional reprogramming factor TBX3.
papers.summary: Adding TBX3 to standard porcine iPSC reprogramming, with transgene-free lines established via WNT inhibition, yielded cells expressing both SSEA-1 and SSEA-4, rapid silencing of exogenous factors, and teratomas containing all three germ layers. Optimized protocols differentiated these iPSCs into smooth muscle, endothelial, hepatocyte-like, and beating cardiomyocytes, expanding agricultural and regenerative applications.

papers.title: The H19/miR-760/BST2 regulatory axis sustains breast cancer tumorigenesis and metastasis.
papers.summary: Long noncoding RNA H19 upregulated BST2 in breast cancer, and BST2 reciprocally modulated H19 in a cross-regulatory loop. miR-760 directly targets both H19 and BST2, coordinating their expression; the H19/miR-760/BST2 axis enhances tumor aggressiveness in vitro and tumor growth in vivo, offering candidate therapeutic targets.

papers.title: ADP-Ribosylation Factor Guanine Nucleotide Exchange Factor 3 Aggravates Cisplatin-Induced Acute Kidney Injury by Impairing Mitochondrial Fatty Acid Oxidation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: ARFGEF3 was upregulated in tubular epithelial cells after cisplatin exposure; knockout in mice attenuated kidney injury, preserving mitochondrial ultrastructure and fatty acid oxidation. Mechanistically ARFGEF3 directly interacted with PGC-1alpha, impeding mitochondrial biogenesis; the PGC-1alpha agonist ZLN005 rescued damage, positioning the ARFGEF3-PGC-1alpha axis as a nephrotoxicity target.

papers.title: ADP Inhibits Macrophage Senescence via the AMPK/KLF10 Pathway in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In systemic lupus erythematosus models, ADP activated AMPK and reduced macrophage senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype release, alleviating disease. ADP promoted KLF10, which binds SIRT1 to deacetylate the CDKN1A promoter, reducing p21. The ADP-AMPK/KLF10 pathway thus limits macrophage aging and may be targetable in lupus nephritis.

papers.title: G Protein-Coupled Receptor 68 Promotes the Progression of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Cuproptosis Resistance via the MEK/ERK Signaling Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: GPR68 was identified as a cuproptosis-associated gene highly expressed in triple-negative breast cancer. Knockdown suppressed growth, migration, invasion, and resistance to copper-induced death via glutaminase regulation; GPR68 overexpression increased ERK phosphorylation, and trametinib blocked these effects, implicating the GPR68-MEK/ERK-GLS axis in cuproptosis resistance and tumor progression.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Collagen Microenvironment Activates NF-κB/Stat3 Axis to Promote Cancer Chemoresistance and Partial EMT in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Three-dimensional collagen culture activated NF-kappaB-Stat3 signaling in head and neck squamous carcinoma cells, upregulating ALDH1A1, ABCG2/BCL2, and a partial EMT program, and increased paclitaxel and cisplatin IC50. NF-kappaB inhibition with PDTC restored chemosensitivity and enhanced paclitaxel efficacy in xenografts; p65 enrichment at tumor-stroma interfaces correlated with nodal metastasis.

papers.title: Metformin Inhibits Trophoblast Ferroptosis by Suppressing ATF2 and Activating the PI3K/Akt/Nrf2 Pathway to Improve Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In gestational diabetes models, metformin suppressed ATF2, reactivating PI3K/Akt signaling, driving NRF2 nuclear translocation and GPX4 upregulation, thereby curbing high-glucose-induced trophoblast ferroptosis. ATF2 overexpression or pathway inhibitors reversed protection, and metformin alleviated placental ferroptosis in hyperglycemic rats, illuminating a ferroptosis-based mechanism in placental metabolic disease.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Reveal Senescent Fibroblast-Associated ADAMTS2 as a Critical Indicator of Intestinal Inflammation in IBD.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Single-cell profiling of inflammatory bowel disease identified highly senescent fibroblasts with pro-inflammatory secretory phenotypes and enhanced communication. Multi-omics integration with an ensemble of 113 machine-learning algorithms prioritized ADAMTS2 as a diagnostic indicator, elevated in patients; senescence-model fibroblasts upregulated ADAMTS2, and knockdown attenuated senescence and fibrosis-associated genes.

papers.title: Deletion of the PDZ-Binding Motif of TAZ Protein Induces Myocardial Calcium Overload and Hypertrophy via the TBX5-MFN2 Signaling Axis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Deletion of TAZ's PDZ-binding motif, a pathogenic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy mutation, blocked TBX5-mediated transcriptional activation of mitofusin 2 (MFN2), triggering cardiomyocyte calcium overload and hypertrophy. TBX5 overexpression was cardioprotective in vivo, reducing heart size, fibrosis, and calcium overload, effects reversed by the TAZ mutation, delineating a TBX5-MFN2 axis in hereditary cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: GCN5-Mediated Lactylation of YY1 Promotes Diabetic Cardiomyopathy by Activating Twist1-Dependent EndMT.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: GCN5-mediated lactylation of YY1 at lysine 203 enhanced YY1 phosphorylation (Thr398), activating Twist1 transcription and driving endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition under high glucose. Endothelial-specific Gcn5 deletion reversed cardiac dysfunction and fibrosis in diabetic mice, defining a GCN5-YY1-Twist1 lactylation axis as a therapeutic target for diabetic cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Ceapin-A7 Suppresses UPR Signaling and Mitigates Retinal Neovascularization in Vldlr(-/-) Mice.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Intramavitreal delivery of the selective ATF6 inhibitor Ceapin-A7 in Vldlr-/- mice reduced ectopic retinal vascular projections and improved scotopic b-wave amplitudes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing showed suppressed ATF6/UPR and angiogenic programs in endothelial cells plus reduced Muller gliosis, supporting ATF6/UPR signaling as a druggable target for neovascular retinal disease.

papers.title: Selective MicroRNA Dysregulation in IPF-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Suggests Restricted Regulatory Remodeling.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Lung mesenchymal stromal cells from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients showed a restricted microRNA program rather than broad reprogramming: only miR-373-3p, miR-486-5p, and miR-449a were downregulated, driving upregulation of profibrotic genes (SMAD4, BCL2, TGF-beta, CXCL12, VEGF), TGF-beta cascade activation, altered autophagy, and proangiogenic signaling.

papers.title: Retbindin Dynamically Redistributes to Preserve Retinal Flavin-Dependent Homeostasis in Response to Riboflavin Availability and Circadian Demand.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Retbindin, a retina-specific riboflavin-binding protein, dynamically redistributes between the outer segment-RPE interface and cone-associated domains in response to riboflavin availability and the light-dark cycle, without changes in total protein abundance. This spatial adaptation preserves flavin-dependent homeostasis and may protect cone function under fluctuating energetic demand.

papers.title: HDAC5 in β-Cells Contributes to the Improvement of Glucose Metabolism Induced by Alternate Day Fasting.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Alternate day fasting upregulated HDAC5 in pancreatic beta-cells, suppressing RASA3 expression, which reduced beta-cell proliferation, increased insulin secretion, and improved glucose metabolism. HDAC5 deficiency abrogated fasting's metabolic benefits, and RASA3 overexpression reversed HDAC5 effects, identifying a fasting-mimetic drug target for glucose homeostasis.

papers.title: SRSF1 Maintains Sertoli Cell Proliferation and Survival by Regulating Alternative Splicing in Coordination With DDX5 and RBMX/RBMXL1.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Sertoli cell-specific SRSF1 ablation arrested proliferation, increased apoptosis, and caused progressive germ cell loss and male infertility. SRSF1 regulated CDK and BAX/BCL2 pathway transcription and formed spliceosomal complexes with DDX5 and RBMX/RBMXL1 to control alternative splicing of CIDEA and RIF1, establishing SRSF1 as a multifunctional spliceosomal hub in spermatogenesis.

papers.title: ADSC-Exosomes Preserve Mitochondrial Function and Ameliorate Uranyl Acetate-Induced Nephrotoxicity Through Inhibition of ATF4 and Activation of PGC-1α/NRF/Tfam Pathway.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) directly suppressed PGC-1alpha transcription during uranyl acetate nephrotoxicity; ATF4 silencing restored mitochondrial biogenesis and cristae architecture. Adipose-derived stem cell exosomes inhibited ATF4, reactivating PGC-1alpha/NRF/Tfam signaling, reducing uranium accumulation, oxidative stress, and renal damage, identifying the ATF4/PGC-1alpha axis as a therapeutic pathway.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing-Based Identification of Novel Podocyte Injury-Associated Genes From Isolated Glomeruli of Diabetic db/db Mice.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing of magnetically isolated glomeruli from diabetic db/db mice identified four podocyte-injury candidate genes (OPCML, ADM, NELL2, DHRS3). In palmitate-stressed human podocytes, OPCML or ADM knockdown and DHRS3 overexpression attenuated apoptosis and preserved actin cytoskeletal integrity, pointing to new therapeutic targets in diabetic kidney disease.

papers.title: A Novel Dual Therapy for Diabetic Ischemic Heart Injury: Sinomenine and Liraglutide Restore Mitochondrial Homeostasis and Suppress Pyroptosis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In diabetic rats with myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, combined sinomenine and liraglutide improved cardiac function, reduced infarct size and troponin I, attenuated NLRP3-driven pyroptosis, enhanced PINK-1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, and reduced oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokines. Mitochondrial division inhibitor pretreatment largely abrogated cardioprotection, supporting mitophagy as a key mechanism.

papers.title: Exosomes From Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Suppress Ferroptosis and CD8(+) T Cell Effector Function in Gastric Cancer via miR-4435/NDUFA10 Axis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Cancer-associated fibroblast exosomes delivered miR-4435, highly expressed in gastric cancer tissues and linked to advanced stage, which targeted NDUFA10 mRNA, suppressing ferroptosis and CD8+ T cell effector function. Exosomal miR-4435 knockdown restored antitumor immunity and enhanced anti-PD-1 sensitivity, nominating miR-4435 as a therapeutic target in gastric cancer.

papers.title: Ellagic Acid Enhances RSL3-Induced Ferroptosis by Inhibiting the Nrf2/HO-1 Signaling Pathway in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Ellagic acid synergized with the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3 in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, amplifying ferroptotic markers and suppressing tumor growth by activating p38 MAPK, promoting KEAP1 upregulation, suppressing NRF2 nuclear translocation, and reducing HO-1. This natural polyphenol overcomes redox adaptation, offering a translatable ferroptosis-potentiating strategy.

papers.title: FABP1-Mediated Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming Buffers Lipotoxicity in Nephrolithiasis via Maintaining PPARγ Activity.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: In nephrolithiasis, crystal-induced lysosomal stress activates calcium/calcineurin signaling, driving TFEB nuclear translocation and FABP1 transcription. FABP1 acts as a nuclear chaperone for PPARgamma, sustaining lipid droplet biogenesis and buffering lipotoxicity; its deficiency precipitates lipid peroxidation and inflammatory injury, and rosiglitazone-mediated PPARgamma activation rescued tubular injury.

papers.title: Interferon Regulatory Factor 1 Inhibits the Adipogenic Differentiation of BMSCs via the AMPK-mTOR Signaling Axis and Induces Their Autophagy to Alleviate Osteoporosis-Related Bone Marrow Adiposity.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Interferon regulatory factor 1 (IRF1) inhibited adipogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells via the AMPK-mTOR axis while inducing protective autophagy. IRF1-overexpressing cells reduced bone marrow adiposity when transplanted into osteoporotic mice, suggesting IRF1 as a therapeutic target for osteoporosis-related marrow adiposity and abnormal adipose metabolism.

papers.title: AMPK/Autophagy-Dependent Pro-Adipogenic Effect Coupled With Enhanced Lipid Mobilization and Thermogenesis Underlies the Dual Action of Canagliflozin Against Obesity.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Canagliflozin promoted preadipocyte differentiation through AMPK-dependent autophagy, yet in vivo reduced obesity via stage-specific lipid mobilization: in differentiated adipocytes it enhanced glycerol release, reduced triglycerides, and increased thermogenesis with elevated mitochondrial proton leak, independent of SGLT2. This reprogramming of lipid turnover explains its dual pro-adipogenic yet anti-obesity action.

papers.title: Oxygen Consumption Rate-Defined Phases Couple Metabolism to Matrix Dynamics in Chondrocyte-Mesenchymal Stromal Cell Co-Culture.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Continuous oxygen-consumption-rate monitoring of nasal chondrocyte-mesenchymal stromal cell co-cultures revealed reproducible tri-phasic respiratory trajectories matching condensation, matrix synthesis, and maturation phases. Chondrocyte-rich mixes accelerated hyaline matrix production, MSC-rich mixes increased stiffness with hypertrophic risk, positioning OCR as a non-destructive, in-process bioenergetic control metric for cartilage engineering.

papers.title: Disulfiram Attenuates Adenine-Induced Renal Fibrosis by Modulating Inflammatory and Immunometabolic Responses.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Disulfiram, an approved alcohol-dependence drug, attenuated adenine-induced renal fibrosis by suppressing inflammatory cell infiltration, inflammasome and pyroptosis markers, and restoring disrupted fatty acid metabolism, while alleviating DNA damage and cellular senescence. Gasdermin D activation in human chronic kidney disease biopsies correlated with severity, supporting disulfiram's immunometabolic relevance to CKD.

papers.title: LILRB4 Recruits SHP-1 to Enhance Oxidative Stress and Apoptosis, Aggravating Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Cardiac LILRB4 overexpression exacerbated ischemia-reperfusion injury by recruiting SHP-1, inhibiting PI3K-NRF2 signaling, suppressing STAT3 phosphorylation, and enhancing oxidative stress and apoptosis; knockout reduced injury and infarct size. LILRB4 thus aggravates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury and may be a therapeutic target.

papers.title: S100A1 Promotes MDM2-Mediated KLF15 Ubiquitination to Regulate ID1-Driven Tubular Injury in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: S100A1 was upregulated in proximal tubules of diabetic kidney disease patients, correlating with proteinuria and renal function. S100A1 promoted MDM2-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of KLF15, relieving KLF15 repression of ID1 and aggravating tubular injury; tubule-specific S100A1 knockdown attenuated injury, inflammation, and fibrosis in diabetic mice.

papers.title: Integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation to Identify Shared Sialylation-Related Signatures in Emphysematous and Fibrotic Lung Disease.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Integrative analysis of COPD, emphysema, and pulmonary fibrosis transcriptomes identified shared molecular signatures, prioritizing the sialylation-related gene ST6GALNAC5, enriched in epithelial cells. Experimental validation showed reduced ST6GALNAC5 and lectin binding in lungs with combined emphysematous-fibrotic injury, and ST6GALNAC5 overexpression attenuated bleomycin-induced epithelial cell injury.

papers.title: Relaxin-2: Shaping the Proteomic Landscape of Skeletal Muscle Physiology, Glucose Trafficking, and Mitochondrial Function in Rat.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Two weeks of serelaxin (recombinant relaxin-2) in healthy rats reshaped skeletal muscle proteomics, decreasing 95 and increasing 32 proteins, including myogenesis, mitochondrial electron transport chain, and glucose metabolism components, plus 35 proteins exclusive to treated muscle. Relaxin-2 thus influences muscle physiology and energetic metabolism relevant to myopathy and cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Identifying JAK2 and ANXA5 as Key Genes Linking Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Oxidative Stress via Machine Learning and Multilayer Transcriptomic Integration With Functional Validation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Integrating bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with machine learning identified JAK2 (upregulated) and ANXA5 (downregulated) as oxidative-stress genes linking obstructive sleep apnea to inflammation, with high diagnostic accuracy (AUC >0.85) in monocytes. Virtual knockout and clinical validation implicated downstream S100P, ALOX5AP, PROK2, and PADI4 in immune-inflammatory regulation.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota-Derived Short-Chain Fatty Acids Driven by N-Carbamylglutamate Alleviates Premature Ovarian Failure Through Suppressing Ferroptosis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: N-carbamylglutamate alleviated cyclophosphamide-induced premature ovarian failure by activating the NRF2/xCT/GPX4 axis and suppressing ovarian ferroptosis. Fecal microbiota transplantation confirmed gut microbiota mediation; NCG increased Lactobacillus abundance and short-chain fatty acids, which exerted anti-ferroptotic effects, highlighting a gut-ovary axis in reproductive aging.

papers.title: Deubiquitinase USP48 Promotes Gastric Cancer Peritoneal Metastasis by Stabilizing S100A9 to Drive Neutrophil Extracellular Traps Formation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: USP48 was overexpressed in gastric cancer, highest in peritoneal metastasis, correlating with poor prognosis. USP48 deubiquitinated and stabilized S100A9, whose secretion activated RAGE/TLR4 on neutrophils to induce neutrophil extracellular traps that drive peritoneal metastasis; USP48 knockdown suppressed tumor growth, NET formation, and metastasis in vivo.

papers.title: Insights Into Spatial Transcriptomics: Exploring Recent Technical Developments and Their Diverse Applications.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: A review of spatial transcriptomics technologies compares four primary approaches, their applications in development and disease, and challenges including sample-type dependence, gene-resolution limits, commercial feasibility, and comprehensive single-cell data capture. It highlights spatial transcriptomics' role in integrated multi-omics and disease modeling while contemplating future technical advances.

papers.title: Toxoplasma gondii SIR2A Promotes Tachyzoite Invasion via Lysine Deacetylase Activity.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Toxoplasma gondii SIR2A, a cytoplasmic NAD+-dependent lysine deacetylase with cell cycle-dependent expression, promotes tachyzoite invasion; conditional depletion impairs invasion, and catalytic-site mutation (H228) elevates global acetylation and compromises invasion. Acetyl-proteomics implicates gene expression, translation, and the ER chaperone TgBiP as substrates, making TgSIR2A a potential drug target.

papers.title: Protein O-Glycosylation Shapes Lymphatic Endothelia and Lymph Node Macrophage Populations.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Inducible deletion of Cosmc or ST3GAL-1 in lymphatic endothelial cells shortened O-glycans, remodeling the endothelial glycocalyx including podoplanin, CD44, LYVE-1, and ICAM-1. These changes were sensed by adhesion molecules such as Siglec-1 and altered lymph node macrophage population size and phenotype, establishing O-glycosylation as a regulator of lymphatic endothelium and immune differentiation.

papers.title: Identification of Sodium/Myo-Inositol Transporter 1 as a Major Determinant of Arterial Contractility.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Sodium/myo-inositol transporter 1 (SMIT1) modulates arterial contractility: knockdown enhanced vasoconstrictor responses and impaired vasorelaxation, while increasing SMIT1 membrane abundance hyperpolarized arteries and augmented KV7-channel-mediated relaxation. SMIT1-KV7.4/7.5 complexes and SGK1 regulation coordinate with Gbeta-gamma subunits, identifying SMIT1 as a key determinant of vascular reactivity.

papers.title: Lipidomic Remodeling by HILPDA in Granulosa Cells Impairs Ovarian Reserve Through Disruption of Mitochondrial and Endoplasmic Reticulum Homeostasis.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: HILPDA was upregulated in granulosa cells from diminished ovarian reserve patients, correlating with reduced ovarian reserve and worse assisted reproduction outcomes. In mice, ovarian HILPDA overexpression promoted follicular atresia; in vitro, it drove triglyceride-rich lipid droplet accumulation, cardiolipin depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ER stress, with lipolysis restoration alleviating dysfunction.

papers.title: A Novel Reporter Mouse for Astrocyte-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Reveals Enrichment of Cargo at Neuronal Mitochondria.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: A novel reporter mouse (Aldh1l1-Cre; CD9-tGFP) fluorescently labels astrocyte-derived extracellular vesicles in vivo. Labeled vesicles associated with capillaries and neurons, with STED microscopy and mitochondrial isolation showing preferential cargo enrichment at neuronal synaptic mitochondria (3-fold higher puncta density), validating a tool for tracking astrocyte-to-neuron EV communication in brain.

papers.title: Immune markers mediate genetic relationships between immune diseases and psychiatric disorders.
papers.summary: Genomic structural equation modeling across 11 immune-mediated diseases and 13 psychiatric disorders found immune markers, especially interleukin-6 rather than C-reactive protein, genetically mediate immune-psychiatric relationships. Six immune markers significantly mediated 11 such associations, including IL-6 accounting for 60% of the genetic link between internalizing disorders and Crohn's disease.

papers.title: C. elegans dauer morphogenesis requires inhibition of DBL-1/BMP signaling by ztf-30.
papers.summary: The zinc-finger transcription factor ZTF-30 is dispensable for C. elegans dauer developmental arrest but essential for dauer morphogenesis: mutants form partial dauers lacking a thickened cuticle and alae, with precocious adult collagen expression and elevated DBL-1/BMP signaling. Reducing DBL-1/BMP rescued the phenotype, establishing active BMP inhibition as required for dauer morphogenesis.

papers.title: Blood flow coordinates collective endothelial cell migration during vascular plexus formation and promotes angiogenic sprout regression via flt4.
papers.summary: In zebrafish, blood flow coordinates collective endothelial cell migration during vascular plexus remodeling, opposing ventral migration and driving regression of non-perfused angiogenic sprouts whose cells migrate against flow and incorporate into the vein. Under low flow, sprout regression requires Flt4, revealing how hemodynamics sculpt vascular networks via endothelial collective migration.

papers.title: Laminin-triggered integrin signaling potentiates γ-enolase-induced neurite outgrowth.
papers.summary: A synthetic C-terminal gamma-enolase peptide induced neurite outgrowth in neuroblastoma and pheochromocytoma cells, with laminin providing the strongest enhancement. Gamma-enolase increased beta-1 integrin surface expression and FAK phosphorylation, with ERK1/2 and AKT activation in a cell type- and ECM-dependent manner, and integrin blockade attenuated neurite outgrowth, implicating laminin-integrin signaling in neurotrophic activity.

papers.title: Evaluation of receptor-interacting protein kinases (RIP1 and RIP3) in the therapeutic effect of thymoquinone against rat testis ischemia/reperfusion.
papers.summary: In rat testicular torsion-induced ischemia/reperfusion, thymoquinone regulated RIP1/RIP3 necroptosis signaling, improved spermatogenic parameters, seminiferous tubule morphology, and hormone profiles (GDNF, ABP, StAR, testosterone, LH), suggesting thymoquinone improves structural and functional tissue integrity after ischemia/reperfusion, though findings warrant confirmation with varied doses and application times.

papers.title: Anti-inflammatory activity of Chlorella polysaccharide AHP.
papers.summary: Chlorella polysaccharide AHP reduced reactive oxygen species, apoptosis, and pro-inflammatory cytokines in dextran sulfate sodium-injured Caco-2 cells and, in mice with DSS colitis, alleviated colon pathology, enhanced tight junction proteins, and repaired the mucosal barrier, while modulating gut microbiota composition and metabolites, supporting bioactive polysaccharides as IBD-directed functional-food candidates.

papers.title: A β-importin supports fusome growth and distribution in Drosophila ovarian germ cells.
papers.summary: The beta-importin TNPO-SR, though not localizing to fusomes, is required for proper fusome morphogenesis in Drosophila ovarian germ cells. Its depletion disrupts microtubule organization and the localization of microtubule-associated protein ASP, and it genetically interacts with cytoskeletal regulators, linking nuclear transport machinery to germline cyst architecture and oocyte specification.

papers.title: Transposon-Induced Paramutation in Maize.
papers.summary: Paired Ac/Fac transposable elements in maize induced heritable paramutation of the p1-rr gene. Inducing and silenced alleles were enriched for small RNAs and cytosine methylation, and unique DNA junctions corresponding to circular inter-transposon segments were detected, supporting reversed-ends transposition generating extrachromosomal circular DNA whose transcription drives trans silencing via small RNAs and methylation.

papers.title: A novel Drosophila ALP/Enigma protein binds to Alpha-actinin to promote sarcomere assembly.
papers.summary: Uchmaz, a novel Drosophila ALP/Enigma family PDZ-domain protein, localizes to Z-discs, associates with alpha-actinin, and requires alpha-actinin for Z-disc targeting. Knockout flies are viable but flightless with fragmented, misaligned Z-discs and reduced alpha-actinin accumulation, illuminating conserved Z-disc assembly mechanisms relevant to human muscular dystrophy and myofibrillar myopathy.

papers.title: Distinct Mitochondrial States Modulate α-Synuclein Toxicity.
papers.summary: In yeast models, fermentative growth kept alpha-synuclein membrane-bound and non-toxic, whereas respiratory growth induced cytoplasmic accumulation, mitochondrial abnormalities, and toxicity. Disrupting respiration also enhanced toxicity despite little accumulation, and HAP4 overexpression suppressed toxicity only with functional mitochondria, showing distinct mitochondrial states modulate alpha-synuclein toxicity in Parkinson's disease models.

papers.title: Excess p50 induces Arp1-dependent dynactin clusters containing the assembly factor VezA.
papers.summary: Overexpressed p50 in Aspergillus nidulans induced ARP1-dependent clusters containing ARP11, p50, and the dynactin assembly factor VezA, trapping VezA in an assembly intermediate lacking the intact shoulder. A conserved p50 beta-sheet region forming contact with ARP1 was critical for clustering, illuminating dynactin assembly and p50's role in neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Reference-Based Cell Type Deconvolution Using Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning in Spatial Transcriptomics with Ctdecon.
papers.summary: Ctdecon is a self-supervised, contrastive-learning neural network module for reference-based cell-type deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics, using scRNA-seq references and spatial correlation of cell types to resolve heavily mixed signals within individual spots. It yields spatially resolved cell-type proportion maps with robustness to technical noise, matching traditional methods' consistency.

papers.title: AZP2006 in Parkinson's disease models: A promising new neuroprotective treatment involving lysosomal homeostasis and the Progranulin/Prosaposin complex.
papers.summary: AZP2006 (ezeprogind), a lysosomotropic neuroprotective molecule in clinical development for progressive supranuclear palsy, counteracted mitochondrial injury and alpha-synuclein preformed fibril toxicity in Parkinson's disease models. Its neuroprotection required progranulin, engaging the progranulin/prosaposin complex to restore lysosomal homeostasis and support dopaminergic neuronal health.

papers.title: A Homozygous Frameshift Variant in KHDC4 Is Associated With a Syndromic Inherited Retinal Disease in Humans.
papers.summary: A homozygous frameshift variant in KHDC4 (c.1535_1538del) segregated with a syndromic inherited retinal disease in a consanguineous family. Mutant protein showed aberrant subcellular localization in vitro, and a zebrafish knockout exhibited mild retinal dysfunction, establishing KHDC4 as a novel candidate gene for syndromic inherited retinal disease.

papers.title: Computational and biophysical validation of tobramycin targeting Mycobacterium MetE(Rv1133c): implications for anti-tuberculosis activity & rifampicin synergy.
papers.summary: Tobramycin binds Mycobacterium tuberculosis methionine synthase MetE (Rv1133c) with high affinity (isothermal calorimetry), inducing conformational perturbations and showing in vitro anti-mycobacterial activity at concentrations non-toxic to human macrophages. It synergized with rifampicin, reducing required concentrations of both drugs and providing a preclinical basis for repurposing tobramycin against multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.

papers.title: Photobiomodulation alters base excision repair gene expression in an experimental model of arthritis.
papers.summary: Photobiomodulation with an 830-nm low-power laser modulated base excision repair gene expression in zymosan-induced arthritis in mice, reducing APE1, FEN1, and LIG1 transcript levels at 24-48 hours and increasing LIG1 at 72 hours. These findings suggest photobiomodulation alters DNA repair pathway activity in inflammatory joint disease.

papers.title: DNA damage response associated miRNA dysregulation in Ataxia-telangiectasia.
papers.summary: In ataxia-telangiectasia fibroblasts, DNA damage response-associated microRNAs showed selective dysregulation: miR-34a-5p and miR-26a-5p were most consistently altered at baseline, whereas bleomycin responsiveness was heterogeneous and cell-line specific. Network analyses of candidate miRNAs identified targets in cell-cycle regulation, RB/E2F, p53 signaling, apoptosis, and senescence, refining ATM-dependent miRNA biology in genome instability.

papers.title: Intraflagellar transport-20 guides the ciliary membrane trafficking of channelrhodopsin in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii.
papers.summary: Intraflagellar transport protein IFT20 co-localized with channelrhodopsin-1 throughout Chlamydomonas flagella, and motor mutants disrupted its anterograde or retrograde movement, trapping cargo near the basal body or ciliary tip. IFT20 acts as a central adaptor interfacing ARF, IFT complex, and BBSome components, with GTP binding inducing concentration-dependent fluorescence quenching in an atypical non-canonical mode.

papers.title: Functional characterization of genetic variants associated with rare inherited renal disorders in the Sri Lankan population.
papers.summary: Whole-exome sequencing of Sri Lankan patients with rare inherited renal disorders identified variants in AVPR2, DAAM2, OCRL, CLCN5, NPHS2, and COL4A5. RT-qPCR and protein modeling showed downregulation of DAAM2, OCRL, CLCN5, and AVPR2, upregulation of NPHS2 and COL4A5, and predicted structural disruption in truncating variants, supporting variant reclassification and population-specific functional data.

papers.title: Microenvironmental Extracellular Matrix Remodeling Driven by GATA2 and GATA3 Deficiency Impairs Lymphatic Recanalization.
papers.summary: GATA2 deficiency impairs lymphatic recanalization after lymph node removal, associated with collagen accumulation. RNA-seq, histology, and immunostaining in Gata2 and Gata3 double heterozygous mice revealed extracellular matrix disorganization, reduced elastin fibers and fibroblasts, and a patchwork dermal phenotype, implicating microenvironmental ECM structure in lymphatic repair and lymphedema.

papers.title: Histochemical staining optimization of a sperm chromatin dispersion test for the evaluation of DNA fragmentation in bovine spermatozoa.
papers.journal: Biotechnic & histochemistry : official publication of the Biological Stain Commission
papers.summary: Sperm chromatin dispersion testing for bovine sperm DNA fragmentation was optimized across nine histochemical stains. Most stains failed to produce consistent chromatin halos, whereas specific modifications of May Grunwald-Giemsa, Feulgen & Rossenbeck, and hematoxylin & eosin yielded reproducible halos, with Feulgen & Rossenbeck avoiding nonspecific background, improving diagnostic reliability in bovine fertility assessment.
